headline: A 2022 law changes the wording of a federal threats statute so it uses gender-neutral terms like spouse instead of wife and widow when protecting former presidents' families.
what_it_does: The law updates a federal criminal offense involving threats to kill, kidnap, or harm a former President or a member of a former President's immediate family. It replaces the gender-specific words wife and widow with the gender-neutral terms spouse and surviving spouse. The summary describes this as a wording change and does not describe any other change to the offense.

who_it_affects.group: Spouses and surviving spouses of former Presidents
who_it_affects.how: The statute now covers them using gender-neutral language, so a former President's husband or widower is clearly included in the protected immediate family.
Their immediate family members are protected under the same threat offense, now worded in gender-neutral terms.

when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a separate effective date; the law was enacted on December 27, 2022.
